description: We are the MacWin team, and winning is our only goal🤫
summary:
Satellite data is public, but finding the right observations and understanding what they mean can take time and specialist tools. Earth Evidence makes that first step easier.

Our browser-based workspace helps users choose a location and dates, search for NASA–ISRO NISAR observations, explore prepared terrain and image views, and keep findings connected to their sources. We start with Tajikistan and a guided flood case in Chókwè, Mozambique, using NASA-published radar images.

Users can compare observations, follow source links, and record research notes. The platform separates what the images show from what still needs investigation.

For Dancing with the SARs, we make radar observations easier to explore without requiring users to build their own interface. This prototype supports research and learning; it does not predict disasters, measure flood depth, or replace field checks. In future, we want to expand coverage and explore additional flood and wildfire data.
details:
Earth Evidence helps people explore satellite observations without spending hours looking for the right images and sources. Choose a place and date range, search the NISAR catalogue, and see what observations are available. Our first focus is Tajikistan, alongside a documented flood case in Chókwè, Mozambique.

The atlas includes prepared satellite image sequences and terrain views. In the Chókwè case, users can compare NASA-published NISAR images, read the evidence report, follow the original sources, and save research notes. A live catalogue match shows that a product exists; it does not mean its pixels have been processed by our tool.

We combine NASA NISAR imagery and ASF catalogue information with Sentinel-1 and Copernicus terrain data. We used AI tools to assist with code, interface text, and review, and identify AI-assisted material in the project.

Earth Evidence is a research prototype, not an emergency warning system. Coverage varies by place and date; the images do not establish flood depth, safe routes, or a validated forecast. In future, we want to expand the approach to more flood cases and explore wildfire data, with independent validation before making hazard predictions.
